To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Over exercise is common in eating disorders, 2) Compulsive exercise has a neurochemical basis and is associated with poorer outcome, and 3) Management of over activity and compulsive exercise is vital in the treatment of eating disorders.

• Over activity is common, but often unrecognized and unmanaged in people with eating disorders, and is a powerful factor in maintaining the disorder • Compulsive exercise is a distinct clinical phenomenon, and is associated with poor prognosis, chronicity, and increased risk of relapse • Assessment of exercise and activity is essential to the management of eating disorders, and should be included from the outset • The management of over activity is complex, but is a key part of the treatment of eating disorders.
